* nixos-configuration

[[https://deepwiki.com/takeokunn/nixos-configuration][https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepWiki-takeokunn%2Fnixos--configuration-blue.svg?logo=data:image/png;base64,]]

** Target

| machine          | name     | os      | system         | stable |
|------------------+----------+---------+----------------+--------|
| Mac M4 Max       | M4-Max   | OSX     | aarch64-darwin | ◎      |
| Thinkpad X13Gen2 | X13Gen2  | NixOS   | x86_64-linux   | ◎      |
| Android OPPO-A79 | OPPO-A79 | Android | aarch64-linux  | △      |

** Usage
*** for M4-Max
#+begin_src shell
  sudo nix run nix-darwin --extra-experimental-features 'flakes nix-command' -- switch --flake .#M4-Max --show-trace
#+end_src
*** for X13Gen2
#+begin_src shell
  sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#X13Gen2 --show-trace
#+end_src
*** for OPPO-A79
#+begin_src shell
  nix-on-droid switch --flake .#OPPO-A79 --show-trace
#+end_src

** Getting the Repository for Development

The commands above apply this configuration to a host in a single shot. For ongoing development (editing, testing, opening PRs), this repository is managed as a bare git clone plus a set of worktrees rather than a single working tree.

Clone it as a bare repository with [[https://github.com/x-motemen/ghq][ghq]] (installed via ~pkgs.ghq~, see [[file:home-manager/vcs/basic.nix][home-manager/vcs/basic.nix]]):
#+begin_src shell
  ghq get --bare <repository-url>
#+end_src
This repository sets git's ~ghq.root~ to ~~/ghq~ (see [[file:home-manager/vcs/git/default.nix][home-manager/vcs/git/default.nix]]), so the clone lands under that directory with no working tree of its own.

Create a worktree to actually edit in, either manually:
#+begin_src shell
  git worktree add <path> <ref>
#+end_src
or with the bundled ~fzf_ghq~ fish function (bound to Ctrl-O, see [[file:home-manager/shell/fish/functions/fzf_ghq.fish][home-manager/shell/fish/functions/fzf_ghq.fish]]), which lists repositories via ~ghq list --full-path~, detects bare repositories, and lets you pick an existing worktree or create a new one under ~.worktrees/<timestamp>-<short-sha>~, then opens a tmux session in it.

Serena memories and Claude settings are shared across a repository's worktrees via a ~.state/~ directory linked into each new worktree, so editor/agent context carries over between them.

** Testing

Elisp regression tests for the Emacs config live in [[file:home-manager/editor/emacs/tests/][home-manager/editor/emacs/tests/]] (standalone ERT suites, not wired into CI). Run one manually with:
#+begin_src shell
  emacs --batch -l home-manager/editor/emacs/tests/gnus-face-cycle-and-modeline-darwin-gate-test.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
#+end_src
